      (∀ t : ℝ, 2 ≤ t → ∀ x : Space, F (t, x) = 0) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, ∀ x : Space, iteratedFDeriv ℝ n F (1, x) = L x n) ∧
      (∀ m : ℕ, ∀ K : ℝ, 0 ≤ K → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
        ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → ∀ x : Space, ∀ directions : Fin m → Fin 4, ∀ j : Fin 3,

            (fun i => CompactForceDecay.spacetimeCoordinate (directions i))) j| ≤
            C * (1 + t) ^ (-K))

findings.summary: No declaration was found stating that the candidate's force has support in K×[0,2]; the exported candidate keeps only compact support in t>0. For the explicit force of NavierStokesR3.ActualCandidate.of_localized_fields, two public lemmas give support in [1/16,21/16]×outerSupport, and outerSupport strictly contains the exported K.

Proof-route difference only. Lean's force is timeCutoff·outerCutoff·F, with F the Taylor–Borel extension of the periodized, time-activated residual. The paper applies series (10.11) to the R³ limits F_j. The stated extension property is unchanged.
(10.5) defines f for 0 ≤ t < 1; Lean's navier_stokes clause covers t ∈ (0,1) only. This is a documented encoding choice, and agreement at t = 0 follows from the exported statement.
PAIRING skeptic's bookkeeping note. Not a paper–Lean difference, so it is dropped as a finding. The three citation corrections are right and are applied in this ruling.

theorem exists_smooth_periodic_extension_of_limits {T : ℝ} {f : SpaceTime → V}
    {J : SpaceTime → FormalMultilinearSeries ℝ SpaceTime V}
    {L : Space → FormalMultilinearSeries ℝ SpaceTime V}
    (hzero : ∀ z : SpaceTime, z.1 < T → (J z 0).curry0 = f z)
    (hderiv : ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ z : SpaceTime, z.1 < T →
      HasFDerivAt (fun y => J y n) (J z (n + 1)).curryLeft z)
    (hlim : ∀ n : ℕ, TendstoLocallyUniformly (fun t x => J (t, x) n)
      (fun x => L x n) (𝓝[<] T))
    (hperiod : ProblemStatement.UnitSpatialPeriodsOn (Iio T) f) :
    ∃ F : SpaceTime → V, ContDiff ℝ ∞ F ∧
      EqOn F f (SpacetimeEndpoint.openPast T) ∧
      ProblemStatement.UnitSpatialPeriodsOn univ F ∧
      (∀ t : ℝ, T + 1 ≤ t → ∀ x : Space, F (t, x) = 0) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ x : Space, iteratedFDeriv ℝ n F (T, x) = L x n

Lean proves this equivalent to the paper's one-sided (X,η) sense (contDiffOn_descend, extension_contDiff/extension_eq). For fields, Lean fields are total on ℝ×ℝ³, so 'extends smoothly across r=0 for t<1' is written inline as ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ on Iio 1 ×ˢ univ. findings.summary: No single Lean def names 'regular at the axis'. The scalar sense has named predicates (GlobalSlowProfiles.Regular, SlowRecursion.Regular). The field sense is written inline as ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ on Iio 1 ×ˢ univ of total Cartesian fields. This is an encoding choice, not a gap.

Lean's scalar encodings are two-sided: ContDiffOn on an open RadialDomain containing the axis, or ContDiff on ℝ². The paper asks for a one-sided extension to X=0. The two are equivalent, and Lean proves the extension step.

The paper (p.27) says Q_s, N_s are axis-regular in the scalar sense of Def 3.2. Lean proves them smooth only for X≠0, and Prop 4.2's residual theorem is stated only off the axis. This is a use of Def 3.2, not the definition itself.

Lean's scalar predicate is even smoothness in the signed radius R, with X=R²/2, rather than one-sided (X,η)-smoothness. The two are equivalent: Whitney descent and the radial extension are proved in Lean, and the converse is composition with R²/2.

Skeptic claim: Lean proves field-sense axis regularity only for the Borel-summed base u_B, not for u^(0). findings.summary: No single declaration states Proposition 4.10. The cone certificate's only existence theorems give one W (NominalConeAssembly.exists_certificate), built at Λ = Λ0, C = C0. Its ingredients are stated for every C ≥ C0 and any radius floor (MatchingConeBounds.exists_ordered_prepared_continuation); the uniform certificate is not stated.

The auditor said (4.33) appears only for an upstream activated stress and that the bounds are unstated. In fact W's own T0 equals activationStress W on the first collar, which has an EdgeFactor with c = t1², and generic lemmas give both bounds.

In Lean's (4.33), the leading coefficient at y=0 is fixed only by a positive first component and a direction. The paper's B_a(0,η)=F(X_a,η)𝔰(X_a,η) is not stated, and the 1/y^order prefactor's order is hidden by an existential, so smooth g_a with g_a(0)>0 is not literal.

No declaration states η-analyticity of the matched profile's fields (f, U, Π, V0/X and their radial derivatives) on one complex neighbourhood over [0, X_an]. Witness and Certificate have no analyticity clause.

The auditor said T0 = 0 is stated only for X ≤ X_a/2. That is wrong. For the nominal Witness, T0 = 0 on (0, X_a] (closed), at X = 0 by formula, and on [0, X_a] for the final witness. (4.13) holds on (0, X_a), and the endpoint follows by continuity.

The ordered choice (j, then Λ, then T_sh and C0, then every C ≥ C0) and the closing sentence (X_R → ∞ with Λ and T_sh fixed) are stated for the full matched Witness. The auditor omitted this and called large_nominal the closest.

All three voters agree, and I checked the cited code myself. Existence comes from the ActualSlowAxis.fromNatural instance of exists_local_slow_hierarchy. It gives one radius and one complex tube around [−1,1] for every n, which is stronger than the paper's order-dependent neighbourhoods. It also gives (5.2)–(5.6) on 0<X≤endpoint·e^δ, zero axis values for all five stored components, joint C^∞ profiles and η-holomorphy of every mixed jet. Uniqueness is positive_solution_unique for system (5.7), which matches the paper's own proof; it lives only in PaperAdditionalResults, off the main chain. stepRaw/stepComponent_profile ties that theorem to the hierarchy. Four residual differences, all low severity: the uniqueness class is stated for (5.7) rather than for profiles; the inner-collar placement of a is missing; the recursion takes uncut lower orders; and the generic theorem is vacuous when U = ∅.

The paper feeds order n the finalized lower orders, with their cutoffs and moment corrections. The Lean hierarchy feeds it its own uncut inner lower orders, so on (X_keep, a²] it solves a different recursion. The per-order theorems accept any regular lower history.

The generic exists_local_slow_hierarchy does not require [−1,1] ⊂ U. With U = ∅ every LocalHierarchy field except `starts` is vacuous. The content comes from the ActualSlowAxis instance, where U contains a fixed tube around [−1,1].

- the radial V_0 clause of (5.42);

- the radial and stream part of u_B = u^(0) on I_mean;
- endpoint extensions for T_phys and E_B.

findings.summary: The radial clause of (5.42), D^I(q^{1/2}u_{r,B} − V_0/√(2X)) = O_I(q^{2h}), is stated nowhere. Only q^A u_r = O(q^h) appears, and only in band-chart (EnvelopeJets) form.
(5.43) is stated only at the weaker end of the paper's displayed chain, C q^h ζ δ^{-N}. The sharper C_I q^{2h} ζ δ^{-N_I} is proved internally but never stated.
exists_final_base takes ∀ upper ∃ base, and its flatness clause covers only X ≤ boxRadius W upper. The paper's order (one base, then every X_max) is stated separately in GlobalBaseError.
The tangential estimates of (5.42) are not stated for the final base in the (q,X,η)/D^I form. They exist as a generic lemma and as band-chart transports, each needing hi ≤ boxRadius W upper.

(5.44) is partly stated: q^A u_θ = c(1+η²)^{-1}X^{-1/2-λ} and q^A u_z = 0 on the mean window. The full u_B = u^(0), including the radial and stream part, is not stated. actual_leading_eq does not reach I_mean, which lies below nominalOuterX.
Endpoint extensions across η = ±1 (t = 1, x ≠ 0) are stated, as smooth extensions, only for u_B and p_B. None is stated for T_phys or E_B.

Clause (f), u_B − u^(0) and p_B − p^(0) vanishing for X ≥ X_+ < X_b, is stated in ActualBaseVelocityBounds/ActualBasePressureBounds.actual_leading_eq on X > nominalOuterX. It is not in exists_final_base, whose heat EqOn starts at nominalExteriorRadius > X_b.

Periodicity and vanishing off the shell are a separate predicate, MovingField; band-chart compatibility is StateOn. No single predicate bundles them.

The auditor claimed no single Lean strip fixes every datum of (6.23)/(6.24). That is false. nativeStrip, which is ActualInitialMean.strip and geometry.strip, fixes ε = Q^h, S = max(1,ℓ²), the flat ζ and the log δ, and differentiates in physical R.

On the actual strip the shell variable is r = R/√q̃ = √(2X), not X. Hence a_a = 4cL = edgeExponent, a_b = 4, δ_Lean = min(1, ½log(X/X_a), ½log(X_b/X)) ∈ [δ/2, δ], and S = max(1, ℓ²). All of these are equivalent up to constants.

I read p.67 and the Lean source myself. torusCovering is J_g on column vectors, and Sheet d = Z²/J^d Z² has index 14^d. The preimage of nativeRectangle (a sup-norm square) is a disjoint union of sheets, each mapped bijectively onto R_γ, and there are 14^gap ≤ 14^Δmax of them. Normalized Haar integrals are invariant under the cover for continuous f, and measure preservation covers every integrable f. ‖J^{±d}‖ ≤ coveringBound D for d ≤ D. Radial integration, averaging and inversion preserve periodicity in H. The auditor and both skeptics agree, and no skeptic raised a missed finding. The verdict is DELTA/partial only because no declaration bundles the lemma and two trivial sub-claims of (d) are unstated. All findings are low severity.

findings.summary: No single declaration states Lemma 6.2, and no docstring cites it. Clauses (a)–(c) are each stated faithfully, (c) and (b) at least as strongly as the paper, across TorusCoverDegree, TorusAverages and CommonCoverSolve/CommonCoverClass.

Two sub-claims of clause (d) have no Lean statement: that torus translation preserves common-torus descent, and that the operations introduce no new dyadic band. Both are trivial, and the second is built into the architecture through an explicit common index.

Cover-pullback naturality of directional inversion is proved only for v_t. For v_r, only Z²-periodicity in the common variable H is stated. That is the Lean encoding of common-torus descent, and radial inversion is never used outside TorusInverse.lean.

I read pp. 69-72 and the Lean sources. The weighted-bound algebra holds: sums, (6.30), both cases of (6.31), all (6.32) rows and the harmonic stages. For C=M the operator rows are concrete, through MeanIncrementBounds.OperatorBounds.{dr,dz,slowTime,fastTime} instantiated by CommonBaseContext.operator_bounds. This refutes auditor finding 3. Cross-label vanishing has derived disjointness (LabelSumBounds.supported_cross_product_zero). Label-uniform versions live in LabelSumBounds.UniformClass. Several gaps remain. The classes record bounds only: no support, no (6.20) compatibility, and θ-independence holds only through the type. Nothing states the pre-cutoff local zero-harmonic mean bound, and no single declaration states the proposition. So the relation is partial and the verdict DELTA. These are gaps in what is stated, not errors.

findings.summary: The Lean bound classes (MemClass, MeanClass, WaveClass) carry only smoothness and weighted bounds on the open domain. Support, torus periodicity and (6.20) compatibility are stated separately, with their own closure lemmas, including for the (6.32) operators. No class predicate conjoining them was found.

No single declaration states Proposition 6.6, and nothing cites it or (6.30)-(6.32). Its clauses are spread over about 20 lemmas in WeightedClasses, LabelSumBounds, MeanIncrementBounds, WaveInteractionBounds, LinearWaveBounds, HarmonicSourceSupport and LocalizedWaveBounds.

The (∂^I w_γ)(∂^J w_γ')=0 form is not stated, but a faithful zero-order form is. supported_cross_product_zero gives u_l·v_k≡0 on the open lift of U for distinct labels, with disjointness derived from SlotSystem, not assumed.

The auditor claimed that the −ε∂_T and Q^{1+h}N_abs rows of (6.32) exist only as abstract instantiations. This is false: concrete operator lemmas exist, and actual chart operators discharge their hypotheses.

The concrete (6.32) operator lemmas tied to the chart context take MeanClass only. For C=W the rows hold through general-weight lemmas, which hold for any w including √ζP, and OperatorBounds discharges their hypotheses.

No lemma states that before the cutoff a zero harmonic satisfies the mean bounds on its labelled rectangle, i.e. LocalWave·LocalWave → LocalMean. The local class exists, contrary to the auditor's note that labels and rectangles are not modelled.

The auditor's MemClass lemmas are uniform in band and point only. The paper requires constants uniform in label and rectangle copy, and that version is stated in LabelSumBounds.UniformClass and LocalClass.

findings.summary: The Lean bound classes (MemClass, MeanClass, WaveClass) carry only smoothness and weighted bounds on the open domain. Support, torus periodicity and (6.20) compatibility are stated separately, with their own closure lemmas, including for the (6.32) operators. No class predicate conjoining them was found.

No single declaration states Proposition 6.6, and nothing cites it or (6.30)-(6.32). Its clauses are spread over about 20 lemmas in WeightedClasses, LabelSumBounds, MeanIncrementBounds, WaveInteractionBounds, LinearWaveBounds, HarmonicSourceSupport and LocalizedWaveBounds.

The (∂^I w_γ)(∂^J w_γ')=0 form is not stated, but a faithful zero-order form is. supported_cross_product_zero gives u_l·v_k≡0 on the open lift of U for distinct labels, with disjointness derived from SlotSystem, not assumed.

The auditor claimed that the −ε∂_T and Q^{1+h}N_abs rows of (6.32) exist only as abstract instantiations. This is false: concrete operator lemmas exist, and actual chart operators discharge their hypotheses.

The concrete (6.32) operator lemmas tied to the chart context take MeanClass only. For C=W the rows hold through general-weight lemmas, which hold for any w including √ζP, and OperatorBounds discharges their hypotheses.

No lemma states that before the cutoff a zero harmonic satisfies the mean bounds on its labelled rectangle, i.e. LocalWave·LocalWave → LocalMean. The local class exists, contrary to the auditor's note that labels and rectangles are not modelled.

The auditor's MemClass lemmas are uniform in band and point only. The paper requires constants uniform in label and rectangle copy, and that version is stated in LabelSumBounds.UniformClass and LocalClass.

I read pp. 69-72 and the Lean sources. The weighted-bound algebra holds: sums, (6.30), both cases of (6.31), all (6.32) rows and the harmonic stages. For C=M the operator rows are concrete, through MeanIncrementBounds.OperatorBounds.{dr,dz,slowTime,fastTime} instantiated by CommonBaseContext.operator_bounds. This refutes auditor finding 3. Cross-label vanishing has derived disjointness (LabelSumBounds.supported_cross_product_zero). Label-uniform versions live in LabelSumBounds.UniformClass. Several gaps remain. The classes record bounds only: no support, no (6.20) compatibility, and θ-independence holds only through the type. Nothing states the pre-cutoff local zero-harmonic mean bound, and no single declaration states the proposition. So the relation is partial and the verdict DELTA. These are gaps in what is stated, not errors.

findings.summary: The Lean bound classes (MemClass, MeanClass, WaveClass) carry only smoothness and weighted bounds on the open domain. Support, torus periodicity and (6.20) compatibility are stated separately, with their own closure lemmas, including for the (6.32) operators. No class predicate conjoining them was found.

No single declaration states Proposition 6.6, and nothing cites it or (6.30)-(6.32). Its clauses are spread over about 20 lemmas in WeightedClasses, LabelSumBounds, MeanIncrementBounds, WaveInteractionBounds, LinearWaveBounds, HarmonicSourceSupport and LocalizedWaveBounds.

The (∂^I w_γ)(∂^J w_γ')=0 form is not stated, but a faithful zero-order form is. supported_cross_product_zero gives u_l·v_k≡0 on the open lift of U for distinct labels, with disjointness derived from SlotSystem, not assumed.

The auditor claimed that the −ε∂_T and Q^{1+h}N_abs rows of (6.32) exist only as abstract instantiations. This is false: concrete operator lemmas exist, and actual chart operators discharge their hypotheses.

The concrete (6.32) operator lemmas tied to the chart context take MeanClass only. For C=W the rows hold through general-weight lemmas, which hold for any w including √ζP, and OperatorBounds discharges their hypotheses.

No lemma states that before the cutoff a zero harmonic satisfies the mean bounds on its labelled rectangle, i.e. LocalWave·LocalWave → LocalMean. The local class exists, contrary to the auditor's note that labels and rectangles are not modelled.

The auditor's MemClass lemmas are uniform in band and point only. The paper requires constants uniform in label and rectangle copy, and that version is stated in LabelSumBounds.UniformClass and LocalClass.

findings.summary: The Lean bound classes (MemClass, MeanClass, WaveClass) carry only smoothness and weighted bounds on the open domain. Support, torus periodicity and (6.20) compatibility are stated separately, with their own closure lemmas, including for the (6.32) operators. No class predicate conjoining them was found.

No single declaration states Proposition 6.6, and nothing cites it or (6.30)-(6.32). Its clauses are spread over about 20 lemmas in WeightedClasses, LabelSumBounds, MeanIncrementBounds, WaveInteractionBounds, LinearWaveBounds, HarmonicSourceSupport and LocalizedWaveBounds.

The (∂^I w_γ)(∂^J w_γ')=0 form is not stated, but a faithful zero-order form is. supported_cross_product_zero gives u_l·v_k≡0 on the open lift of U for distinct labels, with disjointness derived from SlotSystem, not assumed.

The auditor claimed that the −ε∂_T and Q^{1+h}N_abs rows of (6.32) exist only as abstract instantiations. This is false: concrete operator lemmas exist, and actual chart operators discharge their hypotheses.

The concrete (6.32) operator lemmas tied to the chart context take MeanClass only. For C=W the rows hold through general-weight lemmas, which hold for any w including √ζP, and OperatorBounds discharges their hypotheses.

No lemma states that before the cutoff a zero harmonic satisfies the mean bounds on its labelled rectangle, i.e. LocalWave·LocalWave → LocalMean. The local class exists, contrary to the auditor's note that labels and rectangles are not modelled.

The auditor's MemClass lemmas are uniform in band and point only. The paper requires constants uniform in label and rectangle copy, and that version is stated in LabelSumBounds.UniformClass and LocalClass.

findings.summary: The Lean bound classes (MemClass, MeanClass, WaveClass) carry only smoothness and weighted bounds on the open domain. Support, torus periodicity and (6.20) compatibility are stated separately, with their own closure lemmas, including for the (6.32) operators. No class predicate conjoining them was found.

No single declaration states Proposition 6.6, and nothing cites it or (6.30)-(6.32). Its clauses are spread over about 20 lemmas in WeightedClasses, LabelSumBounds, MeanIncrementBounds, WaveInteractionBounds, LinearWaveBounds, HarmonicSourceSupport and LocalizedWaveBounds.

The (∂^I w_γ)(∂^J w_γ')=0 form is not stated, but a faithful zero-order form is. supported_cross_product_zero gives u_l·v_k≡0 on the open lift of U for distinct labels, with disjointness derived from SlotSystem, not assumed.

The auditor claimed that the −ε∂_T and Q^{1+h}N_abs rows of (6.32) exist only as abstract instantiations. This is false: concrete operator lemmas exist, and actual chart operators discharge their hypotheses.

The concrete (6.32) operator lemmas tied to the chart context take MeanClass only. For C=W the rows hold through general-weight lemmas, which hold for any w including √ζP, and OperatorBounds discharges their hypotheses.

No lemma states that before the cutoff a zero harmonic satisfies the mean bounds on its labelled rectangle, i.e. LocalWave·LocalWave → LocalMean. The local class exists, contrary to the auditor's note that labels and rectangles are not modelled.

The auditor's MemClass lemmas are uniform in band and point only. The paper requires constants uniform in label and rectangle copy, and that version is stated in LabelSumBounds.UniformClass and LocalClass.

findings.summary: The Lean bound classes (MemClass, MeanClass, WaveClass) carry only smoothness and weighted bounds on the open domain. Support, torus periodicity and (6.20) compatibility are stated separately, with their own closure lemmas, including for the (6.32) operators. No class predicate conjoining them was found.

No single declaration states Proposition 6.6, and nothing cites it or (6.30)-(6.32). Its clauses are spread over about 20 lemmas in WeightedClasses, LabelSumBounds, MeanIncrementBounds, WaveInteractionBounds, LinearWaveBounds, HarmonicSourceSupport and LocalizedWaveBounds.

The (∂^I w_γ)(∂^J w_γ')=0 form is not stated, but a faithful zero-order form is. supported_cross_product_zero gives u_l·v_k≡0 on the open lift of U for distinct labels, with disjointness derived from SlotSystem, not assumed.

The auditor claimed that the −ε∂_T and Q^{1+h}N_abs rows of (6.32) exist only as abstract instantiations. This is false: concrete operator lemmas exist, and actual chart operators discharge their hypotheses.

The concrete (6.32) operator lemmas tied to the chart context take MeanClass only. For C=W the rows hold through general-weight lemmas, which hold for any w including √ζP, and OperatorBounds discharges their hypotheses.

No lemma states that before the cutoff a zero harmonic satisfies the mean bounds on its labelled rectangle, i.e. LocalWave·LocalWave → LocalMean. The local class exists, contrary to the auditor's note that labels and rectangles are not modelled.

The auditor's MemClass lemmas are uniform in band and point only. The paper requires constants uniform in label and rectangle copy, and that version is stated in LabelSumBounds.UniformClass and LocalClass.

These are gaps in what is stated, not errors.

findings.summary: The Lean bound classes (MemClass, MeanClass, WaveClass) carry only smoothness and weighted bounds on the open domain. Support, torus periodicity and (6.20) compatibility are stated separately, with their own closure lemmas, including for the (6.32) operators. No class predicate conjoining them was found.

No single declaration states Proposition 6.6, and nothing cites it or (6.30)-(6.32). Its clauses are spread over about 20 lemmas in WeightedClasses, LabelSumBounds, MeanIncrementBounds, WaveInteractionBounds, LinearWaveBounds, HarmonicSourceSupport and LocalizedWaveBounds.

The (∂^I w_γ)(∂^J w_γ')=0 form is not stated, but a faithful zero-order form is. supported_cross_product_zero gives u_l·v_k≡0 on the open lift of U for distinct labels, with disjointness derived from SlotSystem, not assumed.

The auditor claimed that the −ε∂_T and Q^{1+h}N_abs rows of (6.32) exist only as abstract instantiations. This is false: concrete operator lemmas exist, and actual chart operators discharge their hypotheses.

The concrete (6.32) operator lemmas tied to the chart context take MeanClass only. For C=W the rows hold through general-weight lemmas, which hold for any w including √ζP, and OperatorBounds discharges their hypotheses.

No lemma states that before the cutoff a zero harmonic satisfies the mean bounds on its labelled rectangle, i.e. LocalWave·LocalWave → LocalMean. The local class exists, contrary to the auditor's note that labels and rectangles are not modelled.

The auditor's MemClass lemmas are uniform in band and point only. The paper requires constants uniform in label and rectangle copy, and that version is stated in LabelSumBounds.UniformClass and LocalClass.

All six constructors of that hypothesis take a source class weighted by copyEnvelope, zero off the closed rectangles, so such a source vanishes beyond both pulse endpoints. Proposition 7.2 does not assume that.

Lean covers every clause of Prop 7.2: existence with (7.13) on H_w, tangency, (7.5) with the printed π_m, descent, supports, uniform (7.14)–(7.15) and the one-sided clause. But every route from the paper's source bound to (7.14)–(7.15) assumes a UniformWaveClass whose copyEnvelope weight vanishes off the closed rectangles, and requires smoothness on all of s.domain × Plane. That forces temporal zero extension, which the paper explicitly does not assume. The hypothesis is therefore strictly stronger, so the relation is lean_weaker and the verdict SINGLE_SOURCE_DELTA (medium). The main chain is unaffected via current_source_class. The PAIRING skeptic's ModalControl-based (7.5) and tangency declarations replace the ModalCopyControl ones. Uniqueness only for the projected ODE and bounds only on the open interval stay low.

findings.summary: ParticularCopyBounds.uniform_coefficients_jets, the general bound, assumes frame-level forcing bounds on the closed pulse interval. All six constructors of that hypothesis take a source class weighted by copyEnvelope, zero off the closed rectangles, so such a source vanishes beyond both pulse endpoints. Proposition 7.2 does not assume that.

Uniqueness is proved only among solutions of the projected ODE (7.13), with two-sided derivatives even at the endpoints. Uniqueness among pairs (t_m, π_m) with tangency, zero data and (7.5) is not stated. The converse step is routine.

On the actual chain, the derivative bounds and the joint and one-sided smoothness of t_m and π_m are proved only on the open pulse interval Ioo 0 L, or for κ-localized sums with tsupport κ ⊆ Ioo a b. The paper states the bounds on the closed interval 0≤v≤L_s.

Two encoding choices: the general bound theorem takes frame-level inputs, which scaledControl discharges, and the degrees b'_I, a'_I are merged into one degree p on S·max(1,δ⁻¹). The merge is equivalent because the paper's δ = min{1,…} ≤ 1.
Descent, joint smoothness and the one-sided τ=0 clause are stated for the κ-localized periodized sum, not for the uncut t_m and π_m.

But every route from the paper's source bound to (7.14)–(7.15) assumes a UniformWaveClass whose copyEnvelope weight vanishes off the closed rectangles, and requires smoothness on all of s.domain × Plane. That forces temporal zero extension, which the paper explicitly does not assume. The PAIRING skeptic's ModalControl-based (7.5) and tangency declarations replace the ModalCopyControl ones. Uniqueness only for the projected ODE and bounds only on the open interval stay low.

findings.summary: ParticularCopyBounds.uniform_coefficients_jets, the general bound, assumes frame-level forcing bounds on the closed pulse interval. All six constructors of that hypothesis take a source class weighted by copyEnvelope, zero off the closed rectangles, so such a source vanishes beyond both pulse endpoints. Proposition 7.2 does not assume that.

Uniqueness is proved only among solutions of the projected ODE (7.13), with two-sided derivatives even at the endpoints. Uniqueness among pairs (t_m, π_m) with tangency, zero data and (7.5) is not stated. The converse step is routine.

On the actual chain, the derivative bounds and the joint and one-sided smoothness of t_m and π_m are proved only on the open pulse interval Ioo 0 L, or for κ-localized sums with tsupport κ ⊆ Ioo a b. The paper states the bounds on the closed interval 0≤v≤L_s.

Two encoding choices: the general bound theorem takes frame-level inputs, which scaledControl discharges, and the degrees b'_I, a'_I are merged into one degree p on S·max(1,δ⁻¹). The merge is equivalent because the paper's δ = min{1,…} ≤ 1.
Descent, joint smoothness and the one-sided τ=0 clause are stated for the κ-localized periodized sum, not for the uncut t_m and π_m.

findings.summary: No single declaration states Proposition 8.3. Its clauses are spread over about 20 lemmas, some on a fixed shell (PressureStream, MeanRankUpdate) and some in the moving √q gauge (VariableGaugeMean, GaugeAliasDecay, MovingMomentBounds, GaugeMassPreservation).

(8.13b) and the zero Y-mean of A_0(g_r − ρP) are stated only for a fixed shell with a globally smooth periodic source. The Y-independent clause has a slice lemma and a moving-gauge instance for the rank source, but no general moving-gauge statement.
Δβ ∈ M_{α+1} is stated with the ε factor only for specific sources (temporal stage, rank stage). For a general γ_d ∈ M_α the Lean states only −∂_ZΨ ∈ M_α for a fixed direction w.
Retention of the (Z,T)-projection of the source support is not stated as a support lemma. The Lean states the stronger FiberLocal property; only radial support is stated directly.

The Lean fixes concrete choices the paper leaves free: ρ is a normed ContDiffBump in the middle half of the same [a,b] used for the source shell, and the cutoff is interiorCutoff(a^d, b^d) in the power chart.

Judge-added. Flatness is stated as MeanClass β for every β in chart variables, at the actual radial frequency with periodicity and index-gap hypotheses, not as an O(q^N) bound on physical derivatives.

I read p.153 and the Lean. All three voters agree on verdict and relation, and I keep both. exists_initialTube with InitialTube.regular/all_radial_jets states clauses (i)-(ii) for f = E/√(2X), U, Ubar and Π on one tube chosen before the widths, which is stronger than the paper. ActualSlowAxis.base with base_beta_value adds V_0/X. The cone is initial_cones. (B.30) is natural_activation_direction, tied to the witness by nominal_activation_stress. Reservation is seed_activation, seed_agreement and fields_outside. No single declaration states the corollary, so it stays partial. I found no material difference: every finding is an attribution gap or a convention with a written recovery. Not vacuous: AssembledSlowBase.nominalTube instantiates the tube.

findings.summary: No single declaration states Corollary B.6. exists_initialTube with InitialTube.regular/all_radial_jets gives clauses (i)-(ii); the cone, (B.30), t_c and reservation clauses are stated faithfully by separate Prop B.5, nominal-assembly and modulation declarations.

InitialTube lists f, U, Ubar, Pi rather than V_0/X. But ActualSlowAxis.base carries V_0/X as its fifth component, an AxisFunction on the same complex parameter domain, and base_beta_value identifies it with radialFlux/X, i.e. (4.7).

No declaration states the finite bounds for radial derivatives on a smaller neighbourhood; all_radial_jets concludes only Regular. The bounds follow in one line from continuity on a compact subset of the open domain.

Lean has no named t_c. initial_cones gives a collar t ≤ activationTime ≤ referenceWidth, and the reserved collar X_0·e^{t/2} is chosen inside nominalBounds_of_certificate. The paper's strict t_c and 4e^{t_c} < 4.1 are recovered by shrinking.

The auditor left open whether ActivationCone.activatedStress is the witness's stress. nominal_activation_stress proves it for y ≤ referenceWidth, and modulated_activation_stress carries it to the final modulated profile on the reserved collar.

The auditor's recovery of the reservation clause used only seed_agreement, which misses the Appendix C modulation. Lean covers it: the modulated profile equals W outside (modulation.left, repairPatch.right), with modulation.left > X_0.

natural_activation_direction exports positivity of B_0(0,η) but not the identity B_0(0,η) = F·p_{s,r} of (B.30). exists_actual_stress_direction states the identity, and natural_reference_log_match discharges its matching hypothesis for the natural profile.

findings.summary: We found no single declaration stating that the modulated profile satisfies all of Theorem 4.6. exists_weighted_profile conjoins the open-annulus cone, the bounds (C.19) with the weight (C.18) and two edge collars; stress support and other clauses are separate lemmas about the same witness.

Auditor's sub-claim that (i), (v), (vi) and (4.25) are never restated for v.profiles is overstated. Lean restates the analytic rectangle, exterior pressure, zero exterior mass and both reserved patches for the modified profile.

The edge identities n(X_a) ∥ (a,−b_s) and n(X_b) = (1,0) are stated by no declaration about the modulated stress. The collar lemmas hide the coefficient behind ∃ G and export only positivity and ε-margins.
Auditor's claim that b_s(X_b)=0 is not exported for the modulated profile is wrong: modulated_terminal_shears at x=0 states logShearB v.profiles (η, rightEdge W) = 0, and Lean's shearB is −b_s.

Lean states no single κ∈(0,2) for (4.26) on the closed annulus and no uniform lower bounds for F, a, v_s−2; it has pointwise strict inequalities there, ε-margins on both collars and a continuous closed direction.
